contract: Pure build of one integration/ai-text request from role and skill instructions, selected memory, history and tools in one declared order (one system message, one memory block, one message per history entry, marked content only as rendered blocks), within a caller-supplied token window and estimate and the hard request bounds of ai-text; one declared drop order (oldest unit of a call with its results, then the last memory item) never drops instructions, tools, keep-rule records or the newest unit; older image references become a fixed marked text; with the optional image_input true, only the newest user history entry renders its host-vouched images (0..8 artifact references in the ai-text image rules) as image parts after its text part, other user entries leave their images out, and tool-result and content image references always stay marked reference blocks bounded by max_image_refs; without image_input the request and canonical bytes are unchanged; refusals before any drop, over_limit when nothing is left to drop.
limits: No claim that a provider accepts each order of messages that the inputs allow, and no claim about the accuracy of an estimate; an approximate estimate is returned as approximate.

No other optional member of the ai-text request, image parts only from the newest user entry, by reference (no images in older turns or in compaction, no documents), no template language, no tokenizer, no rule that decides when to compact and no join with a tool registry.
No claim that marking prevents prompt injection; the caller decides what is an instruction and what is content.
Too many tools and a tool description over 4,096 bytes are refused, not cut.

The host vouches that a user entry's images are the person's; only their shape is checked here, and their bytes, hashes and sizes are checked by integration/ai-text at admission and dispatch. Image tokens are not in the caller's estimate unless the caller counts them; integration/ai-token-count refuses a request with parts, so with that estimator an image build is estimate_unavailable. After a tool turn the drop order may remove the newest user entry and its images.

grounding.claim: Named groups drop_order (a two-call unit goes whole, then memory from the last, literal dropped list, over_limit), orphan_tool_result (five refused histories, one with a result for a call that its assistant entry does not hold, no estimate call), hard_bounds (257 messages to 256, 65 tools, descriptions of 4,097 and 4,096 bytes, byte bounds 1,000, 2,000 and 65,536, never-dropped parts alone over a bound), deterministic (one literal canonical text, estimate sees only canonical bytes, approximate and other-estimator values) and image_refs (five references with limits 2 and 0, image, document and parts keys refused) and image_parts (newest user entry as one text part and image parts in order, older entries' images left out, images: [] as text, images without image_input, 9 refs, extra key, bad artifact IDs, versions 0 and 2,147,483,648 and image/svg+xml refused before any drop, 8 refs and each media type accepted, tool-result and content image references stay marked blocks at the max_image_refs edge beside eight image parts, a drop after a tool turn takes the newest user entry's images), the deterministic golden unchanged with image_input false, plus shape refusals; every accepted request passes Request.decode/2 with its bound. A drop that removes an assistant entry without its results, and a tool-result image reference rendered as an image part, are negative controls. Finite scenarios with a byte-size estimate, not a proof.

Pinned Elixir lists and maps; the ready Contracts of integration/ai-text (Request.decode/2 decides what a valid request is and its canonical encoding) and workflow/untrusted-content (decode/1, encode/1, render/1) are reused unchanged.
Pinned Jason encodes the JSON values in Request.canonical/1 and decodes them in Request.decode/2.

The caller decides what is an instruction and what is content: role instructions come from the recipe, skill instructions only from a pinned_skill source, every tool result, document, member message and summary is a truthfully stamped marked value, memory was selected with its access check, a record holds no unmarked content, IDs are unique, and the estimate function is pure and tells its direction truthfully.

telemetry.contract: Pure function emits no observations; the host owns instrumentation.

config.contract: Per call only, supplied by the caller in the input: max_request_bytes 1..65,536 (the host's ai-text request-byte Config), max_image_refs 0..256, image_input (optional boolean, default false), and the token window (size, estimator_id, estimator_version; unit tokens) with the host's estimate function. No default other than image_input false, no ambient or stored setting and no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle to control.
